claims_disputed.claim: Task quality is assured by static validation and rollout-based QC.
claims_disputed.reason: 45 of 115 tasks (39%) still had task-side defects after static validation and were found only through rollouts by three model tiers, so defects those models did not trigger can remain. The review's reading that '~1/3 of initial failures were task defects' is an arithmetic error: Claude-Opus-4.6 went from 19.1% to 30.4% resolved, i.e. 11.3 pp out of 80.9 pp of failures, about 14%. QC gains are also uneven (+11.2 pp for Opus-4.6, +3.0 GLM-5.1, +1.0 Kimi-K2.5), which suggests the repairs favour the strongest QC model.

claims_disputed.claim: Top models are scaffold-robust; mid/low-tier models swing 3–10 pp between OpenHands and Terminus 2.
claims_disputed.reason: I agree with weak and add stronger evidence. The paper's own Terminus numbers for the same models differ between Table 4 'After' (Opus-4.6 30.4, GLM-5.1 20.4, Kimi-K2.5 7.1) and Table 2 (31.3, 20.9, 7.8). Run-to-run noise of about 1 pp is therefore as large as the 0.9 pp 'robustness' gap.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: Every task uses structured roadmap instructions; no condition varies or removes their structure. Partial credit showing agents stall at integration is a capability finding, not evidence that structured acceptance criteria help.

missed_issues: Internal inconsistency on Java: App. G.1 (line 1425) lists the five target languages as Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, but Table 3 contains C++ (Glaze, thread-pool) and no Java repository. The review notes there is no Java but misses that the paper contradicts itself, which bears on how carefully the dataset was described.

QC uses rollouts from the same models that are then ranked (Opus-4.6, GLM-5.1 and Kimi-K2.5 appear in Table 4 and on the leaderboard). This is self-referential benchmark construction (benchmark_overfit), beyond the selection_bias label the review used.
Unequal reasoning effort (xhigh for Opus-4.7, high for four models, default for the rest) is a fairness confound in the configuration, not a metric_mismatch. It favours the top-ranked model directly.
Sloppy citations, e.g. Kimi-K2.6 attributed to 'MiniMax (2026a)'. Tool-call counts for Opus-4.7 are given as both 101 and 102 in §5.2.
Relevance is generous at 3: single-repo OSS version upgrades, no Java, no cross-repo contracts. The useful takeaway (per-target acceptance tests; integration is where agents fail) is indirect.
note: Review is careful and its verdict is right. It contains one arithmetic overreach on the QC table, a P34 'supports' stance without an ablation behind it, and misses that Table 4 versus Table 2 shows run-to-run noise as large as the scaffold-robustness claim.
